profile.campus: Silicon Valley (San Jose/Santa Clara), California (Equinix's founding market, Great Oaks/Corvin/Duane campuses)
profile.reading:
This building is Equinix's SV17 facility, part of Equinix's Silicon Valley data center network in the San Jose/Santa Clara area. Equinix was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, both former Digital Equipment Corporation facilities managers, on the idea of building a neutral place where competing internet networks could physically connect and exchange traffic, a model that let the company grow through network effects as more networks joined; Equinix converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX. Silicon Valley, where Equinix is still headquartered today in nearby Redwood City, was the company's founding market, and its San Jose facilities on Great Oaks Boulevard and its Santa Clara facilities on Corvin Drive and Duane Avenue grew into one of the densest interconnection hubs in Equinix's global network as the company expanded internationally, entering Asia-Pacific in 2002, Europe via the IXEurope acquisition in 2007, Latin America in 2011, and the Middle East in 2013, and opening its 50th global data center in London by 2010 around the time it acquired Switch and Data Facilities Company. Equinix's own published specifications for the flagship SV1 building on this campus describe an 82,850-square-foot, single-story, steel-frame facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 2kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, and generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load; Equinix markets the Great Oaks campus for its direct connections to major networks and tier-1 cloud service providers. Equinix's website did not disclose this specific building's own square footage or power capacity separately from the SV1 figure cited as representative of the broader campus.

Pacific Gas and Electric, the regional utility serving most of Silicon Valley, and Silicon Valley Power, Santa Clara's municipal utility, have both cited sustained data center load growth across the San Jose-Santa Clara-Sunnyvale corridor in their own capacity planning, a dynamic distinct from the newer data center markets elsewhere in the country given how built-out and power-constrained the Bay Area grid already is after decades of continuous data center development since Equinix's own 1998 founding in the area.

reading.body:
Equinix SV17 in Santa Clara is a confirmed active data center facility, but Equinix does not publish its power capacity or investment figures, limiting what can be measured about the building's role in AI infrastructure scaling.

The facility operates as part of Equinix's Silicon Valley metro campus, which claims over 10,500 customers including thousands of enterprises and network service providers. Six independent aggregator sources confirm its address and ongoing operation, even though Equinix's own index pages do not consistently list it. This suggests the company maintains substantial regional capacity without transparent disclosure of per-building metrics.

For tracking compute infrastructure and power constraints, this opacity matters. A data center's existence can be confirmed. Its power draw, cooling capacity, recent expansion, or utilization cannot. Equinix's specification sheets exist but require direct contact to obtain, placing detailed facility analysis outside public research workflows.

The Silicon Valley region hosts multiple Equinix facilities spanning Santa Clara, San Jose, Palo Alto, and Sunnyvale. Without published power figures for individual buildings, total regional capacity remains unmeasured, even for one of the world's largest colocation operators serving the geographic heart of AI development and deployment.
